The children of Adam are limbs of one another, for in creation they are of one essence. When time brings pain to one limb, the other limbs find no rest. You who feel no sorrow for the suffering of others do not deserve to be called human.
Praise be to God, the Mighty and Glorious, obedience to whom brings nearness, and gratitude to whom brings an increase of blessings.
Do not count as a friend the one who, in times of plenty, boasts of friendship and brotherhood. A friend is one who takes a friend by the hand in distress and helplessness.
How well said Ferdowsi, pure of birth — may mercy rest upon his pure grave: do not harm the ant that carries its grain, for it has a life, and sweet life is dear.

He who has knowledge has power; through knowledge an old heart grows young.
Flourishing buildings fall into ruin from the rain and the heat of the sun; I have laid the foundation of a lofty palace of verse that wind and rain will never harm.

Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same.

Your children are not your children. / They are the sons and daughters of Life’s longing for itself.

What does not kill me makes me stronger.

Everything in a person should be beautiful: the face, the clothes, the soul and the thoughts.

I remember a wondrous moment: you appeared before me like a fleeting vision, like the spirit of pure beauty.
There are no weeds and no bad men. There are only bad cultivators.
All human wisdom will be contained in these two words: wait and hope!
We must cultivate our garden.
…the only true voyage… would be not to visit new landscapes, but to have other eyes…

Is it not a pleasure to learn and to practise what one has learned from time to time? Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar?
What you do not wish for yourself, do not do to others.
A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath one’s feet.
The highest good is like water. Water benefits all things and does not compete.
Know the enemy and know yourself, and in a hundred battles you will never be in peril.
When the false is taken for true, the true becomes false; where nothing is taken for something, something becomes nothing.
It is said that the great forces of the world, long divided, must unite; long united, must divide.
In fact, there were no roads on the earth to begin with; when many people walk the same way, a road appears.

The scent of the Muliyan stream comes to me; / the memory of a kind friend comes to me.
Much toil I endured in these thirty years; / I brought Persia back to life with this Persian tongue.
If Iran is not to be, let my body not be; / let no one live on in this land.
Do not blame the azure wheel of the sky; / cast the wind of stubborn pride out of your head.
O King, I speak of You, for You are pure and You are God; / I will walk no road but the one You show me.
Praise to the pure Creator of the soul, / who gave life — and faith — to dust.
Through love, bitter things turn sweet; / through love, copper turns to gold.
I was dead, I came alive; I was tears, I became laughter. / The fortune of love arrived, and I became a lasting fortune.
We are from above, and to above we go; / we are from the sea, and to the sea we go.
I am glad in the world because the world's gladness is from Him; / I love the whole world, for the whole world is from Him.
O camel driver, go slowly — the peace of my soul is leaving; / the heart I had with me is leaving with my beloved.
You whose fifty years are gone while you still sleep — / perhaps you may yet seize these last five days.
Friends, listen to the tale of my distress; / listen to the story of my hidden grief.
They say that when my mother bore me / she taught me to take the breast; / nights beside my cradle / she sat awake and taught me to sleep.
From the blood of the homeland's young, tulips have bloomed; / mourning their cypress-like stature, the cypress has bowed.
O white demon with your feet in chains, / O dome of the world, O Damavand!
O people sitting on the shore, cheerful and laughing — / someone in the water is giving up his life.
The moonlight seeps down, / the glowworm shines; / not for a moment does sleep break in anyone’s eyes, and yet / the sorrow for these few sleepers / breaks the sleep in my wet eyes.
No one will introduce me / to the sun; / no one will take me to the sparrows' party. / Remember the flight — / the bird is mortal.
I speak from the depth of night, / from the depth of darkness / and from the depth of night I speak. / If you come to my house, O kind one, bring me a lamp / and a window through which / I can look at the crowd of the happy street.
I remember the days when I sang my lament in the garden, / when I had a nest among the tulips and the roses.
Shall I compare thee to a summer's day? / Thou art more lovely and more temperate.
Life's but a walking shadow, a poor player / That struts and frets his hour upon the stage / And then is heard no more.
To see a World in a Grain of Sand / And a Heaven in a Wild Flower, / Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand / And Eternity in an hour.
I wandered lonely as a cloud / That floats on high o'er vales and hills, / When all at once I saw a crowd, / A host, of golden daffodils
A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: / Its loveliness increases; it will never / Pass into nothingness
She walks in beauty, like the night / Of cloudless climes and starry skies
My name is Ozymandias, King of Kings; / Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair! / Nothing beside remains.
'Tis better to have loved and lost / Than never to have loved at all.
“Hope” is the thing with feathers - / That perches in the soul - / And sings the tune without the words - / And never stops - at all -
O Captain! my Captain! our fearful trip is done, / The ship has weather'd every rack, the prize we sought is won
Take thy beak from out my heart, and take thy form from off my door! / Quoth the Raven “Nevermore.”
If you can keep your head when all about you / Are losing theirs and blaming it on you
But I, being poor, have only my dreams; / I have spread my dreams under your feet; / Tread softly because you tread on my dreams.
If you shed tears when you miss the sun, you also miss the stars.
Frost and sun — a wonderful day! / Still you are dozing, lovely friend — / it's time, my beauty, wake up.
I loved you; and perhaps this love / has not yet fully died out in my soul.
A lonely sail gleams white / in the blue mist of the sea!.. / What does it seek in a distant land? / What has it left behind at home?..
Russia cannot be understood with the mind, / nor measured with a common yardstick: / she has a special stature — / in Russia one can only believe.
Night, a street, a streetlamp, a pharmacy, / a meaningless and dim light. / Live another quarter century — / it will all be the same. There is no way out.
I do not regret, I do not call, I do not weep; / all will pass, like smoke from white apple trees.
Listen! / If the stars are lit, / it means someone needs them, doesn't it?
I like that you are not sick with love for me, / I like that I am not sick with love for you.
Before my bed, the bright moonlight — / I wonder if it is frost on the ground. / I raise my head and gaze at the bright moon, / I lower my head and think of home.
The country is broken, but mountains and rivers remain; / spring comes to the city, grass and trees grow deep.
The white sun sets behind the mountains, / the Yellow River flows into the sea. / If you want to see a thousand li further, / climb one more storey.
Sleeping in spring, I didn't notice the dawn; / everywhere I hear birds singing. / Last night, the sound of wind and rain — / how many flowers have fallen?
Alone in a strange land, a stranger, / on every festival I miss my family twice as much.
If you have a true friend within the four seas, / the ends of the earth are like next door.
Wildfires cannot burn it all away; / when the spring wind blows, it grows again.
I only wish that we may live long, / and, a thousand li apart, share the beauty of the same moon.
The road ahead is long and far; / I will search high and low.
Softly I am leaving, / just as softly as I came; / softly I wave my hand / to bid farewell to the clouds of the western sky.
Tomorrow, at dawn, at the hour when the countryside whitens, / I will set out. You see, I know that you are waiting for me.
There, all is order and beauty, / luxury, calm and pleasure.
The long sobs / of the violins / of autumn / wound my heart / with a monotonous / languor.
It has been found again. / What? — Eternity. / It is the sea gone off / with the sun.
Under the Mirabeau bridge flows the Seine / and our loves — / must I remember them? / Joy always came after sorrow. / Let night come, let the hour strike; / the days go by, I remain.
There is no use in running; one must set out on time.
Live, if you believe me; do not wait for tomorrow: / gather the roses of life starting today.
O time, suspend your flight! and you, propitious hours, / suspend your course: / let us savour the fleeting delights / of the most beautiful of our days!
Over all the hilltops / is peace; / in all the treetops / you feel / hardly a breath; / the little birds are silent in the forest. / Just wait — soon / you too will rest.
Green, how I want you green. / Green wind. Green branches. / The ship upon the sea / and the horse on the mountain.
An old pond — / a frog jumps in, / the sound of water.
